ideas.name: SlipKey
ideas.niche: Smart maritime access management for private and commercial boat slips.
ideas.problem: The high operational cost of manual staffing for guest access and the security risks/logistical failures of traditional physical key systems in remote, low-connectivity dock environments.
ideas.targetUser: Private boat owners who host frequent guests, marina managers overseeing large-scale slip operations, and maritime service providers (mechanics, cleaners) requiring scheduled, supervised access.
coreFeatures: Timed Digital Credentials (QR and Bluetooth-based temporary access)
Asynchronous Command Queuing (storing access commands to sync when signal returns)
Service Provider Scheduling (pre-authorized windows for maintenance/deliveries)
Live Access Audit Logs (real-time tracking of all gate/slip entries)
realDependencies: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) API for local device communication
MQTT or AWS IoT Core for low-bandwidth remote command relay
Twilio API for SMS-based credential delivery
Google Maps Geofencing API for proximity-based security verification
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will feature a 'Developer Simulation Overlay' containing three toggles: 'Signal Strength' (ranging from 0% to 100%), 'Connectivity Mode' (Online vs. Satellite Lag), and 'Mock Hardware'. The 'Signal Strength' slider will trigger a local state machine: at 0%, all API calls are intercepted and added to a visible 'Pending Sync' queue in the UI. The 'Satellite Lag' mode will inject a randomized 3000ms–8000ms delay into all JSON responses. Bluetooth discovery will be bypassed via a 'Simulated Discovery' button that triggers a 3-second 'Searching...' animation before returning a hardcoded list of nearby 'Smart Locks'.

ideas.name: Isobaric
ideas.problem: The high cognitive load and manual error risk associated with tracking real-time gas consumption, multi-gas switches, and complex decompression profiles during deep-water technical dives.
ideas.targetUser: Advanced technical divers (Trimix/Nitrox) aged 30-55, typically high-income enthusiasts performing deep wreck, cave, or technical exploration dives using multi-cylinder configurations.
coreFeatures: Real-time Gas-Mix HUD Overlay: Live visual telemetry of O2/He fractions and remaining volume per cylinder via BLE.
Dynamic Deco-Stop Recalculation: Real-time adjustment of decompression obligations based on actual gas consumption rates.
Gas-Switch Safety Interlock: Step-by-step digital verification prompts for gas transitions to prevent hypoxia or oxygen toxicity.
Physiological Trend Analytics: Cloud-synced post-dive dashboard for analyzing inert gas loading and off-gassing efficiency over time.
realDependencies: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) Protocol for dive computer/HUD integration
Bühlmann ZHL-16C Decompression Algorithm API
NIST-traceable pressure and depth sensor hardware integration
Cloud-based distributed database (e.g., AWS DynamoDB) for log synchronization
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a 'Scenario Injector' that streams pre-recorded dive profiles through a WebSocket-based mock server. This server will broadcast simulated telemetry (depth, pressure, gas fractions) with randomized 'sensor jitter' to mimic real-world data noise. To emulate hardware latency, a middleware layer will inject a variable 200ms-800ms delay on all BLE-simulated packets. The decompression engine will be replaced by a local JSON lookup table containing pre-calculated profiles for specific depths, while the cloud sync will be simulated using a local Mock API that introduces a 1.5-second artificial latency to mimic intermittent connectivity during surface intervals.

ideas.name: OrthoSync Pro
ideas.niche: Real-time spatial and torque synchronization for orthopedic implant placement.
ideas.problem: The 'Digital Surgery Gap' where manual implant placement deviates from pre-operative 3D digital plans due to a lack of real-time spatial feedback and verification.
ideas.targetUser: Orthopedic surgeons specializing in complex joint reconstructions and surgical navigation technicians in high-acuity hospital operating rooms.
coreFeatures: Real-time 3D Spatial Overlay (Syncing tool orientation to pre-op bone scans)
Live Torque & Depth Telemetry (Visual/Auditory monitoring of screw engagement)
Automated Deviation Analysis (Instant 'Planned vs. Actual' placement reports)
Boundary Proximity Alerts (Visual warnings when drill trajectory nears critical anatomical structures)
realDependencies: DICOM/STL 3D Rendering Engine
Low-latency IoT/Bluetooth SDK for smart drill telemetry
PACS Integration for patient imaging retrieval
Real-time WebSocket/MQTT telemetry stream
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local WebSocket server to broadcast a JSON payload containing simulated XYZ coordinates and Euler angles using a random-walk algorithm to mimic fluid tool movement. Torque will be emulated via a high-frequency data stream that simulates resistance spikes. 3D models will be pulled from a local assets folder rather than a PACS server, and a 'Network Latency Middleware' will be implemented to inject a randomized 50ms-150ms delay into the data packets to simulate real-world wireless interference.

ideas.name: EchoLayer
ideas.niche: High-resolution bathymetric mapping for portable, non-integrated sonar hardware.
ideas.problem: Portable sonar users receive real-time depth data but lack the software to synthesize that data into visual, topographical maps, preventing them from identifying underwater structures and consistent fishing patterns.
ideas.targetUser: Weekend hobbyist anglers and mobile kayak fishers (ages 25-55) who use Bluetooth/Wi-Fi transducers and want professional-grade terrain visualization without the cost of high-end marine chartplotters.
coreFeatures: Live Depth-to-Map Stitching: Automatically converts sequential GPS and sonar pings into a continuous 3D contour map.
Structure Layering: Toggleable visual overlays for bottom composition (rock vs. mud) and vegetation density.
Hotspot Annotator: Drop geo-tagged pins on significant topographic features like drop-offs, ledges, or wrecks with photo attachments.
Offline Terrain Cache: Downloadable local map tiles to allow full mapping functionality in remote areas without cellular service.
Export to GPX/KML: Share high-resolution bathymetric files with desktop mapping software or fellow anglers.
realDependencies: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) or Wi-Fi Direct protocols for transducer communication
Mobile GNSS/GPS hardware for spatial positioning
Mapbox GL JS or Google Maps SDK for topographical base layer rendering
PostGIS or similar spatial database for storing complex geometric map data
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a simulated 'Sonar Streamer' class that emits a WebSocket-like stream of JSON packets containing mock depth, temperature, and battery data. This data will follow a pre-recorded sine-wave pattern to simulate a boat moving over a submerged ridge. GPS location will be emulated by iterating through a hardcoded array of 500 coordinate waypoints that trace a realistic fishing pattern. Instead of real-time computational bathymetry, the app will use a Perlin noise algorithm to generate a 3D mesh that reacts to the mock depth values, providing the visual illusion of real-time map generation. All 'Cloud Sync' and 'Export' actions will include a simulated 1.5 to 3-second delay with a progress bar to mimic network latency and heavy data processing.

ideas.name: DustLogic
ideas.niche: Solar Soiling & Maintenance Optimization for Remote Micro-grids
ideas.problem: Unoptimized cleaning cycles in arid regions lead to either significant energy yield loss due to heavy dust accumulation or wasted operational expenditure from unnecessary manual cleaning.
ideas.targetUser: Operations & Maintenance (O&M) managers and micro-grid asset owners operating in remote, high-dust or desert environments.
coreFeatures: Real-time Soiling Index Dashboard via optical sensor telemetry
Economic ROI Engine (compares lost kWh revenue vs. cleaning service costs)
Predictive Maintenance Forecasting based on local weather/dust patterns
Multi-site Fleet Geospatial Map for remote monitoring
realDependencies: IoT/MQTT sensor data stream from optical hardware
Hyper-local Meteorological API (e.g., OpenWeatherMap or IBM Weather)
Time-series database (e.g., InfluxDB or AWS Timestream)
Geospatial mapping service (e.g., Mapbox)
Financial/ERP integration for localized labor and equipment costs
ideas.emulationStrategy: Implement a mock server that uses a stateful timer to simulate shifting sensor data; 'light_transmittance' values will decrease by a fixed percentage every 'simulated hour' to mimic dust buildup. Use a weather simulator that toggles between 'High Dust' and 'Rain' states to show how the UI reacts to environmental shifts. Inject artificial network latency (800ms to 3000ms) into all mock API responses to simulate the high-latency satellite/cellular connections typical of remote micro-grid locations. Provide a static JSON lookup table for regional cleaning costs to enable the ROI calculation logic to function during the demo.
